angle_en: Sages and Krishna speak the same truth
angle_hi: ऋषि और स्वयं आप एक ही सत्य कहते हैं

en.intro: Arjuna lists the great sages who speak of Krishna this way, and then adds Krishna himself to their number.
en.notice: The verse names sages like Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa, and then adds Krishna himself to their number.
en.next: Arjuna then accepts all of this as true, saying that even the gods do not know your full form.
en.meaning: All the sages speak of you this way: the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa. You yourself also say this to me.

hi.intro: अर्जुन उन महान ऋषियों के नाम बताते हैं जो आपके बारे में ऐसा कहते हैं, और फिर उनमें स्वयं आप भी जुड़ते हैं।
hi.meaning: अर्जुन कहते हैं, सभी ऋषि आपको ऐसे ही कहते हैं, देवर्षि नारद, असित, देवल तथा व्यास। और स्वयं आप भी मेरे प्रति ऐसा कहते हैं।
hi.notice: इस श्लोक में चार ऋषियों के नाम हैं, नारद, असित, देवल और व्यास, और फिर इसमें स्वयं आप भी जुड़ते हैं जो यही बात कहते हैं।
hi.next: अर्जुन यह सब सत्य मानते हैं और कहते हैं कि भगवान, देव और असुर भी आपके रूप को नहीं जानते।

en.intro: Arjuna lists the great sages who speak of Krishna this way, and then adds Krishna himself to their number.
en.body: All the sages speak of you this way: the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa. You yourself also say this to me. The verse names sages like Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa, and then adds Krishna himself to their number. Arjuna then accepts all of this as true, saying that even the gods do not know your full form.

issues: meaning_changed: "और स्वयं आप भी मेरे प्रति ऐसा कहते हैं।" (The Hindi meaning drops the crucial detail that Krishna himself also says this (स्वयं च एव ब्रवीषि मे). It incorrectly implies that Krishna is simply one among the sages, rather than the supreme being who is being quoted by them.)
